name: Tdbengine
tagline: Small German relational database with a built-in EASY language for CGI web apps; descended from DOS TDB.
description: tdbengine came from tdb Software Service GmbH as the successor to its DOS-era TDB database: a roughly 400 KB relational engine with an integrated programming language, EASY, that ran behind a web server through the CGI interface. It handled tables, indexes, full-text indexing, memos and BLOBs and a semaphore scheme for concurrent access, on Linux, FreeBSD and Windows, and had a German-speaking community building CMS, wiki and bug-tracking applications on it in the early 2000s. Version 6.4.03 was the last listed, the community site stopped changing around 2005-2010, and tdbengine.org now redirects elsewhere. tdb Software itself now sells unrelated business software.
statusNote: No releases after 6.4.03; the tdbengine.org community site is gone and the vendor now sells unrelated software. Use SQLite, PostgreSQL or MariaDB.

pricing.notes: Was sold commercially rather than as freeware; no longer offered.

strengths: Tiny footprint with the database and application language in one binary
Built-in full-text indexing and BLOB support
Simple CGI deployment behind any web server
weaknesses: Discontinued; no downloads or support remain
Proprietary EASY language instead of SQL
